title: Lexicographic Digitization and Data Linking Tools
description: This session introduces the infrastructure for lexicographic digitization, focusing on segmentation, content conversion, and alignment tools designed to link data for Linked Open Data. The discussion outlines the tools, existing resources, and the timeline for testing and deployment.
summary:
The presentation introduced the infrastructure for lexicographic digitization, which consists of several sets of tools including automatic segmentation, lexicographic content conversion, and alignment tools. These tools are designed to facilitate the integration and use of data in Linked Open Data. The linking tools are crucial for providing conceptual interoperability.

Existing resources discussed include BabelNet and a proposed quick-and-dirty scenario tool named Alexa Fire. For complete conversion, existing XLT tools can be utilized, though this process is more time-consuming. The discussion emphasized a critical timeline, noting that software pieces will be provided by month 24 (end of January 2020), and a full year will be allocated for conversion tools. The primary goal is to gather the observer community to test the developed tools, with real-world usage anticipated one year after the initial software delivery.

title: Developing a Dictionary Matrix for Semantic Linking
description: This discussion outlines the methodology for creating a "Dictionary Matrix" to link and cross-reference different linguistic entries, such as headwords, senses, and concepts, across various language resources. The goal is to identify specific lemma-sense relationships for deeper semantic understanding.
summary: The discussion focuses on the implementation of a "Dictionary Matrix" (or matrix dictionary) as the primary tool for linking linguistic data. The process involves identifying crucial parts of dictionary entries, including headwords, senses, and examples. The core objective is to manually or programmatically identify connections between different semantic representations—for instance, linking a specific sense in a dictionary (like Longman) to corresponding concepts in resources like WordNet. The method aims to identify "lemma sense" by linking a headword to a specific concept ID, potentially staying at the lemma level or expanding to the concept level (e.g., identifying headwords like "illusia" and "macaroni" from the Slovenian dictionary).

title: Infrastructure Development and Service Planning Timeline
description: This segment outlines the progress and planning for infrastructure development, specifically focusing on the scope of tools and services detailed in the grant agreement. It establishes a timeline where initial services will be available within the first year of the project, leading up to the final completion in 2021.
summary: The discussion focuses on the status of various infrastructure components, noting that the work on the Lex 1 and 3 infrastructure has officially started in February. Existing progress includes Rolex 2, which began in Month 3. The segment highlights that the displayed content covers the proposed ideas and descriptions of tools and services outlined in the grant agreement. A key point is the availability schedule: almost all services will be accessible in the first stage (within one year), with the final completion planned for Month 36 (2021) at the end of the project.

title: Unifying Dictionary Data through Structured Conversion and Linking Infrastructure
description: This discussion outlines the proposed infrastructure (LAX) designed to standardize dictionary data by converting unstructured and legacy resources into a uniform model, leveraging the Elexis Data Model for structural alignment and creating linked open data clouds.
summary: The presentation details the LAX infrastructure, which includes tools for handling retro-digitized dictionaries. It introduces Grobet Dictionaries for parsing and structuring unstructured text, enabling the conversion of various dictionary formats (like Word documents or digitized paper) into a standardized TI like O format. The core process involves using the Elexis Data Model to map custom dictionary elements to a uniform structure, allowing for both basic and full conversion of dictionaries. The ultimate goal is to achieve cross-dictionary linking—integrating results into a European Dictionary Portal to create linguistic linked open data clouds, connecting dictionary entries to concrete resources across platforms like WordNet and BabelNet. The infrastructure relies on Grobet Dictionaries, the Elexis Data Model, and a dictionary matrix/word sense immigration system.
